title: Shift rule for character-weighted sums
statement:
Let $f, g : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be Boolean functions, let $S \subseteq [n]$, and write $\chi_S(x) = \prod_{i \in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ for the associated Walsh character, where $\oplus$ denotes componentwise XOR. Suppose the order of summation may be interchanged in the double sum
\[
  \sum_{x}\Big(\sum_{y} f(y)\,g(x \oplus y)\Big)\chi_S(x)
  \;=\;
  \sum_{y} f(y)\sum_{x} g(x \oplus y)\,\chi_S(x).
\]
Then for every $y \in \{0,1\}^n$, translating the argument of $g$ by $y$ multiplies the character-weighted sum by the factor $\chi_S(y)$:
\[
  \sum_{x} g(x \oplus y)\,\chi_S(x)
  \;=\;
  \chi_S(y)\sum_{x} g(x)\,\chi_S(x).
\]
hypotheses_covered: f and g are Boolean functions on {0,1}^n
the Fubini interchange of summation order holds for the double sum with f, g, chi_S
y is a point of the hypercube {0,1}^n
replaced:
Let $f, g : \{0,1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, let $S \subseteq [n]$, assume the Fubini
interchange for the convolution coefficient, and let $y \in \{0,1\}^n$.  Then
translating the argument of $g$ by $y$ only multiplies the character-weighted sum by
$\chi_S(y)$:
\[
  \sum_{x} g(x \oplus y)\,\chi_S(x)
  \;=\; \chi_S(y) \sum_{x} g(x)\,\chi_S(x).
\]
